notes:
Cloud sync is far safer for projects kept inside Dropbox, OneDrive or iCloud: Corylus no longer stores anything machine-specific inside the project folder, so another computer's search index or sync bookkeeping can no longer overwrite yours. Existing projects migrate automatically the first time you open them.

- Fixed a bug where one interrupted sync could stop a project syncing permanently, with a terminal command as the only way out.
- Fixed a bug that could hide a document in the binder while its file sat safely on disk, most often after syncing between a Mac and a Windows PC. Affected projects repair themselves on the next open.
- Fixed a Windows bug that could lose an edit Corylus had just merged, because the editor kept showing the old text and the next automatic save wrote it back.
- Trashed folders and images are reachable again.
- "Sync now" now publishes this computer's binder structure when the two computers cannot agree which is newer; automatic syncs still leave it alone.
- Your backup folder is remembered per computer instead of travelling with the project.
- Corylus refuses to open a project archive whose contents would be written outside the folder you chose.
